title: The Monotone Feasibility
prompt:
**Scenario.** Split an array into the fewest contiguous parts so each part's sum is ≤ S. Checking a fixed part-count bound greedily is easy. The intended acceleration?

**Which approach is the best fit? The program only needs to print the letter.**

**A)** Binary search on the answer (the maximum part sum) with a greedy feasibility check

**B)** DP over all part boundaries

**C)** Sort the array and greedily group

**D)** Bellman–Ford on a part-graph

tests.name: answer
tests.hint: Wait — the honest framing: feasibility is monotone in the per-part cap C ('parts needed' is non-increasing in C), so binary search C, greedy count. The DP works but is heavier than needed.
